Natural_Language: This part prescribes policies and procedures specifically for research and development (R&D) contracting.

Validation_Notes: Declarative scope statement. Atomic proposition, no logical operators needed.

Natural_Language: As used in this subpart, the following definitions apply.
Atomic_Propositions: P_35_001: Definitions for terms used in Part 35
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition for definitions section. Encompasses applied research and development definitions.

Natural_Language: Applied research means the effort that normally follows basic research, attempts to determine and exploit potential, and attempts to advance the state of the art; excludes efforts aimed at design/development/testing for sale when used in cost principle applications.
Atomic_Propositions: P_35_001_AR: Applied research definition encompasses characteristics and exclusions
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition for applied research definition. All three characteristics plus the exclusion clause collectively define the term.

Natural_Language: Applied research normally follows basic research, but may not be severable from the related basic research.
Atomic_Propositions: P_35_001_AR_1_i_a: Applied research normally follows basic research; P_35_001_AR_1_i_b: Applied research may not be severable from related basic research
Validation_Notes: Advisory 'normally' indicates typical sequence but not absolute requirement. 'May not be severable' uses permissive 'may' to indicate possibility, not certainty, represented as tautology.

Natural_Language: Attempts to determine and exploit the potential of scientific discoveries or improvements in technology, materials, processes, methods, devices, or techniques.
Atomic_Propositions: P_35_001_AR_1_ii: Applied research attempts to determine and exploit potential of scientific discoveries or improvements in technology, materials, processes, methods, devices, or techniques
Validation_Notes: Definitional characteristic. Atomic proposition describing the scope of applied research activities.

Natural_Language: Attempts to advance the state of the art.
Atomic_Propositions: P_35_001_AR_1_iii: Applied research attempts to advance the state of the art
Validation_Notes: Definitional characteristic. Atomic proposition.

Natural_Language: When being used by contractors in cost principle applications, this term does not include efforts whose principal aim is the design, development, or testing of specific items or services to be considered for sale; these efforts are within the definition of 'development,' given below.
Atomic_Propositions: P_35_001_AR_2_a: Contractor is using applied research in cost principle applications; P_35_001_AR_2_b: Principal aim is design, development, or testing of specific items or services for sale; P_35_001_AR_2_c: Efforts are excluded from applied research definition
Validation_Notes: Conditional exclusion: when both conditions (cost principle application AND principal aim is sale) are met, the effort is excluded from applied research. HIGH-RISK because material implication must correctly represent that both conditions are necessary triggers for the exclusion.

Natural_Language: Development means the systematic use of scientific and technical knowledge in the design, development, testing, or evaluation of a potential new product or service (or of an improvement in an existing product or service) to meet specific performance requirements or objectives. It includes the functions of design engineering, prototyping, and engineering testing; it excludes subcontracted technical effort that is for the sole purpose of developing an additional source for an existing product.
Atomic_Propositions: P_35_001_DEV_a: Development is the systematic use of scientific and technical knowledge in design, development, testing, or evaluation of potential new or improved products/services to meet specific performance requirements; P_35_001_DEV_b: Development includes design engineering, prototyping, and engineering testing; P_35_001_DEV_c: Development excludes subcontracted technical effort solely for developing an additional source for an existing product
Validation_Notes: Definitional statement with inclusions and exclusions. The negation represents the explicit exclusion of subcontracted efforts for additional sourcing.

Natural_Language: Policy.
Atomic_Propositions: P_35_002: Policy for R&D contracting covers use of contracts and cost sharing
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition for policy section.

Natural_Language: Contracts must be used only when the principal purpose is the acquisition of supplies or services for the direct benefit or use of the Federal Government. Grants or cooperative agreements should be used when the principal purpose of the transaction is to stimulate or support research and development for another public purpose.
Atomic_Propositions: P_35_002_a_1: Principal purpose is acquisition of supplies or services for direct benefit or use of Federal Government; P_35_002_a_2: Contracts must be used; P_35_002_a_3: Principal purpose is to stimulate or support R&D for another public purpose; P_35_002_a_4: Grants or cooperative agreements should be used
Validation_Notes: Two conditional requirements: (1) mandatory 'must' for contracts when purpose is direct government benefit, (2) advisory 'should' for grants/cooperative agreements when purpose is public R&D support. The second conditional is advisory, not mandatory. HIGH-RISK due to material implication distinguishing mandatory vs. advisory instruments.

Natural_Language: Cost sharing policies (which are not otherwise required by law) under Government contracts must be in accordance with part 16, part 42 and agency procedures.
Atomic_Propositions: P_35_002_b_a: Cost sharing policies are not otherwise required by law; P_35_002_b_b: Cost sharing policies under Government contracts must be in accordance with part 16, part 42 and agency procedures
Validation_Notes: Conditional: when cost sharing is not already required by law, it must follow parts 16, 42 and agency procedures. The parenthetical creates the antecedent condition. HIGH-RISK because the parenthetical qualifier is critical to scope.

Validation_Notes: Parent proposition for the solicitations section. All subsections (a) through (k) collectively define solicitation requirements.

Validation_Notes: Advisory 'should' for both the CO sending solicitations and technical personnel recommending sources. Parent for qualification criteria subsections (1)-(5). Not mandatory but represents best practice guidance.

Validation_Notes: Enumerated qualification criterion. Atomic proposition.

Natural_Language: Proposals must generally be solicited from technically qualified sources, including sources identified through synopses or other means of publicizing requirements. Competition promotion through additional solicitation is mandatory ('must'). The 'may' creates a tautological consequent for the impracticality condition.

Validation_Notes: Mandatory solicitation requirement. Atomic proposition.

Atomic_Propositions: P_35_101_c_4: Offerors must propose any planned subcontracting of scientific or technical work
Validation_Notes: Mandatory solicitation requirement. Atomic proposition.

Natural_Language: Solicitations may require proposals to be organized with technical sections grouped together for efficient review by technical experts (see part 15). Both the solicitation process and proposal evaluation should be designed to reduce costs for both offerors and the Government.
Atomic_Propositions: P_35_101_d_a: Solicitations may require proposals organized with technical sections grouped for efficient review; P_35_101_d_b: Solicitation process and proposal evaluation should be designed to reduce costs for offerors and Government
Validation_Notes: First clause is permissive ('may'), represented as tautology. Second clause is advisory ('should'). Neither is mandatory. Flagged for review due to advisory nature.

Validation_Notes: Parent proposition. Advisory 'should' -- these factors are recommended, not mandatory. The 'such as' phrasing indicates the list is illustrative, not exhaustive.

Atomic_Propositions: P_35_101_e_1: Evaluation factor: offeror's understanding of scope of work
Validation_Notes: Recommended evaluation factor. Atomic proposition.

Natural_Language: The quality of the offeror's approach proposed to meet the scientific and technical objectives, or the merit of the ideas or concepts presented.
Atomic_Propositions: P_35_101_e_2_a: Quality of offeror's approach to meet objectives; P_35_101_e_2_b: Merit of ideas or concepts presented
Validation_Notes: Disjunctive evaluation factor -- either quality of approach OR merit of ideas. The 'or' indicates alternative evaluation criteria.

Natural_Language: The offeror's access to qualified engineering, scientific, or other technical staff.
Atomic_Propositions: P_35_101_e_3: Evaluation factor: offeror's access to qualified technical staff
Validation_Notes: Recommended evaluation factor. Atomic proposition.

Natural_Language: The offeror's experience is relevant.
Atomic_Propositions: P_35_101_e_4: Evaluation factor: offeror's relevant experience
Validation_Notes: Recommended evaluation factor. Atomic proposition.

Atomic_Propositions: P_35_101_e_5: Evaluation factor: innovative ideas in the specific scientific or technical field
Validation_Notes: Recommended evaluation factor. Atomic proposition.

Natural_Language: The offeror's access to the necessary research, testing, laboratory, or shop facilities.
Atomic_Propositions: P_35_101_e_6: Evaluation factor: offeror's access to necessary research, testing, laboratory, or shop facilities
Validation_Notes: Recommended evaluation factor. Atomic proposition.

Validation_Notes: Parent proposition. Mandatory 'must' for considering management capability, though qualified by 'as appropriate.' Sub-factors are conjunctive.

Natural_Language: Management capabilities, including cost control methods.
Atomic_Propositions: P_35_101_f_1: Management evaluation factor: management capabilities including cost control methods
Validation_Notes: Management evaluation sub-factor. Atomic proposition.

Validation_Notes: Management evaluation sub-factor. Atomic proposition.

Natural_Language: Subcontracting practices.
Atomic_Propositions: P_35_101_f_3: Management evaluation factor: subcontracting practices
Validation_Notes: Management evaluation sub-factor. Atomic proposition.

Atomic_Propositions: P_35_101_f_4: Management evaluation factor: other significant evaluation criteria such as unrealistically low cost estimates
Validation_Notes: Catch-all management evaluation sub-factor with illustrative example. Atomic proposition.

Natural_Language: Although cost or price is not usually the deciding factor in selecting a contractor to perform R&D, it remains important. The final selection should be the offer that best satisfies the Government's requirement at a fair and reasonable cost.
Atomic_Propositions: P_35_101_g_a: Cost or price is not usually the deciding factor for R&D contractor selection; P_35_101_g_b: Cost or price remains important; P_35_101_g_c: Final selection should be the offer that best satisfies Government requirement at fair and reasonable cost
Validation_Notes: Advisory provision ('should' for final selection). Establishes that technical merit dominates but cost is still a factor. Best-value determination standard for R&D.

Natural_Language: The contracting officer should ensure potential offerors completely understand the details of the work, especially the Government interpretation of the work statement. For complex requirements, the contracting officer should give potential offerors a chance to comment on the details of the requirements as contained in the work statement, the contract schedule, and any related specifications. This may be done at a preproposal conference (see part 15).
Atomic_Propositions: P_35_101_h_a: CO should ensure potential offerors understand work details and Government interpretation; P_35_101_h_b: Requirements are complex; P_35_101_h_c: CO should give offerors chance to comment on requirements; P_35_101_h_d: CO may conduct a preproposal conference
Justification_Rules: Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Tautology (Taut): Rule 18
Validation_Notes: Mixed advisory/permissive. General understanding is advisory ('should'). Complexity triggers additional advisory requirement. Preproposal conference is permissive ('may'). HIGH-RISK due to conditional on complex requirements.

Natural_Language: When appropriate, solicitations should allow offerors to propose an alternative contract type (see part 16).
Atomic_Propositions: P_35_101_i_a: Circumstances are appropriate; P_35_101_i_b: Solicitations should allow offerors to propose alternative contract type
Validation_Notes: Conditional advisory: when appropriate, solicitations should (not must) allow alternative contract types. Advisory nature combined with conditional trigger. HIGH-RISK due to material implication with subjective 'when appropriate' antecedent.

Natural_Language: When a potential contractor wants to discuss a new idea or product based on their privately-funded independent R&D work, Government personnel should be willing to discuss it. However, the potential contractor must be informed that these discussions do not create any obligation for the Government. In such situations, direct negotiation with the potential contractor without competition may be appropriate. Also refer to part 15 regarding unsolicited proposals.
Atomic_Propositions: P_35_101_j_a: Potential contractor wants to discuss new idea from privately-funded IR&D; P_35_101_j_b: Government personnel should be willing to discuss; P_35_101_j_c: Contractor must be informed discussions create no Government obligation; P_35_101_j_d: Direct negotiation without competition may be appropriate
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Tautology (Taut): Rule 18
Validation_Notes: Complex multi-modal provision: advisory 'should' for willingness to discuss, mandatory 'must' for informing about no obligation, permissive 'may' for direct negotiation. The mandatory element (no obligation disclosure) is unconditional within the scenario. HIGH-RISK due to multiple modal verbs and material implication.

Natural_Language: The Government may issue an exploratory request to identify existing ideas or prior work in a specific field of research. Any such request must clearly state that it does not impose any obligation on the Government or signify a firm intention to enter into a contract.
Atomic_Propositions: P_35_101_k_a: Government may issue exploratory request to identify existing ideas or prior work; P_35_101_k_b: Exploratory request is issued; P_35_101_k_c: Request must clearly state no Government obligation and no firm intention to contract
Justification_Rules: Tautology (Taut): Rule 18; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]
Validation_Notes: Permissive authority to issue exploratory request ('may'), but if issued, mandatory requirement ('must') to include disclaimer. The conditional is triggered by exercise of the permissive authority.

Natural_Language: Broad agency announcement.
Atomic_Propositions: P_35_102: Requirements and procedures for broad agency announcements
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition for BAA section.

Natural_Language: This paragraph prescribes procedures for the use of the broad agency announcement (BAA) with Peer or Scientific Review (see part 6) for the acquisition of basic and applied research, as well as that part of development not related to developing a specific system or hardware procurement. The BAA technique must only be used when meaningful proposals with varying technical/scientific approaches are reasonably expected.
Atomic_Propositions: P_35_102_a_1: BAA prescribes procedures for acquisition of basic and applied research and non-system development; P_35_102_a_2: Meaningful proposals with varying technical/scientific approaches are reasonably expected; P_35_102_a_3: BAA technique is used
Validation_Notes: Scope statement plus mandatory precondition. BAA use is conditioned on expectation of varying approaches. The 'must only be used when' creates a necessary condition: P_35_102_a_2 is required for P_35_102_a_3. Logically equivalent to ~P_35_102_a_2 ⊃ ~P_35_102_a_3. HIGH-RISK due to the conditional restricting use.

Natural_Language: The BAA and its supporting documentation must include specified elements.
Atomic_Propositions: P_35_102_b: BAA and supporting documentation must include all specified elements
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition. Mandatory 'must' applies to all four sub-requirements conjunctively.

Natural_Language: Describe what research the agency is interested in, either for specific program needs or broad areas covering a range of agency requirements.
Atomic_Propositions: P_35_102_b_1: BAA must describe research the agency is interested in for specific program needs or broad areas
Validation_Notes: Mandatory BAA content requirement. Atomic proposition.

Natural_Language: Explain how proposals will be selected, the relative importance of each criteria, and the evaluation methodology.
Atomic_Propositions: P_35_102_b_2: BAA must explain selection process, criteria importance, and evaluation methodology
Validation_Notes: Mandatory BAA content requirement. Atomic proposition.

Natural_Language: Specify the proposal due date.
Atomic_Propositions: P_35_102_b_3: BAA must specify proposal due date
Validation_Notes: Mandatory BAA content requirement. Atomic proposition.

Natural_Language: Contain clear instructions for preparing and submitting proposals.
Atomic_Propositions: P_35_102_b_4: BAA must contain clear instructions for preparing and submitting proposals
Validation_Notes: Mandatory BAA content requirement. Atomic proposition.

Natural_Language: Contracting officers must publicize the BAA through the Governmentwide point of entry (GPE) and, if authorized in accordance with part 5, may also be published in scientific, technical, or engineering periodicals, or other electronic platforms and communities used by the target audience. Publish the notice at least once per year.
Atomic_Propositions: P_35_102_c_a: CO must publicize BAA through GPE; P_35_102_c_b: Publication is authorized per part 5; P_35_102_c_c: BAA may also be published in periodicals or electronic platforms; P_35_102_c_d: Notice must be published at least once per year
Justification_Rules: Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Tautology (Taut): Rule 18
Validation_Notes: Mixed mandatory/permissive. GPE publication and annual frequency are mandatory ('must'). Additional publication in periodicals is permissive ('may') conditioned on part 5 authorization. HIGH-RISK due to conditional permissive element.

Natural_Language: Use a peer or scientific review process to evaluate proposals. Written evaluation reports are required for each proposal; however, proposals are not required to be evaluated against each other since they are responding to broad research areas rather than a common work statement.
Atomic_Propositions: P_35_102_d_a: Peer or scientific review process must be used to evaluate proposals; P_35_102_d_b: Written evaluation reports are required for each proposal; P_35_102_d_c: Proposals are not required to be evaluated against each other
Validation_Notes: Three requirements: mandatory peer review, mandatory written reports, explicit negation of comparative evaluation requirement. The negation reflects BAA's nature as responding to broad research areas.

Validation_Notes: BAA selection criterion. Atomic proposition.

Validation_Notes: Parent proposition for evaluation and award section.

Validation_Notes: Advisory 'should' for award criterion. Best-value standard tempered by proportionality requirement (capabilities should not exceed need). Practical guidance to avoid overspending on capability beyond requirement scope.
